Hi Kimberly / Karthik,

Thanks again for the run-through earlier. We have to pick a connectivity approach for the AcmeBridge Private deployment by end of the month — our security/compliance and SRE teams are split across options (VPC peering, PrivateLink, S2S VPN). Key constraints:
- Data classification: PCI scope for tokenized transactions (must minimize cross-account surface).
- Throughput: Peak of ~2.5 Gbps sustained, spikes to 4-5 Gbps during batch jobs.
- Latency: sub-30ms ideal for API calls, but bulk ingestion can tolerate higher.
- Operational team prefers a low-touch model (avoid frequent route changes).

Could you share Redwood's recommended topology and any tradeoffs (latency/cost/ops) and a preferred mutual action plan? I've attached our current topology image.

Subject: RE: Connectivity options for private deployment (short ask) — initial recommendation + tradeoffs

Jordan / team — thanks. Based on the constraints (PCI-scoped data, 2.5–5 Gbps peaks, low-touch ops), here's a prioritized recommendation and a short tradeoff table. I attached a compact architecture sketch (redwood-recommendation-diagram.pdf) and a CSV with latency/cost numbers.

Recommendation (short):
1) PrivateLink-style private endpoints (Redwood-hosted endpoint service + ENIs in AcmeBridge account) for control plane and low-volume, PCI-scoped traffic. Rationale: least cross-account routing surface (no route table propagation between accounts), works well with customer-managed certs and private DNS.
2) Dedicated VPC peering for high-throughput bulk ingestion paths (if you need sustained multi-Gbps). Rationale: less per-packet overhead vs VPN; predictable throughput and simpler metrics for SRE. Peering requires careful routing table management and potentially an additional Transit setup if you have many VPCs.
3) Site-to-site VPN only as a fallback / temporary dev path or for remote dc-to-dc links. Reason: encryption overhead and variable performance under load; operationally heavier to scale for multi-Gbps long term.

Tradeoffs (high level):
- Latency: Peering ~= lowest latency (single-region, same AZ routing), PrivateLink adds ~1–3ms overhead from ENI hops, VPN can add 10–50ms and varies.
- Throughput: Peering supports higher sustained throughput (subject to inter-account quotas and route propagation). PrivateLink caps per-ENI throughput and will need multiple ENIs/load distribution for sustained multi-Gbps. VPN throughput depends on your appliance and cloud gateway limits.
- Security surface: PrivateLink reduces attack surface by exposing a single endpoint in your account; peering exposes route-level access between CIDR ranges; VPN is encapsulated but terminates outside Redwood’s managed control plane unless you terminate inside.
- Ops & billing: PrivateLink shifts data egress billing/ENI charges (Redwood + AWS PrivateLink costs) vs peering where you may see cross-account transfer but fewer per-connection charges. VPN may have lower transfer cost but high maintenance. Marcus — see attached cost delta (latency-cost-matrix.csv).

Proposed immediate plan (mutual action):
- Week 1: Approve control-plane via PrivateLink (short trial for PCI-scoped API calls).
- Week 2: Provision peering for bulk ingestion path; validate with synthetic load to confirm throughput and latency.
- Week 3: Roll traffic and monitor; fall back to VPN if we hit quota/throughput blockers.

Attachments: redwood-recommendation-diagram.pdf, latency-cost-matrix.csv

Let me know if you want a call tomorrow for 30m to walk the diagram.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Connectivity options for private deployment (short ask) — cost + capacity notes

Jordan / Kimberly / team — quick follow-up with some numbers and ops notes after reviewing your topology and Karthik’s sketch. See summarized bullets below; full CSV attached.

Numbers (ballpark, US-East):
- Peering: supports multi-Gbps; expect ~0.5–1.5ms median added latency inside same AZ; cross-account data transfer depends on AWS account topology (we calculate ~$0.02–0.03 per GB for inter-AZ transfer if routed). No per-connection charge from AWS for peering but possible carrier fees if you use Direct Connect.
- PrivateLink: expect single-ENI baseline throughput ~500–800 Mbps; to reach 3–4 Gbps you'd provision 4–6 ENIs behind a load balancer or use a dedicated accelerated endpoint. Cost estimate (AWS & Redwood infra): ~$0.06–0.12 per GB for endpoint data + ENI hourly charges; operationally simpler for compliance.
- VPN: variable; to hit 2–4 Gbps you'd need high-end appliances or multiple tunnels + BGP. Managed VPN appliances add monthly costs and more ops overhead.

Ops notes:
- If AcmeBridge wants private certs and cert rotation inside your control plane, PrivateLink is easiest for attesting TLS termination inside your account.
- For peering, plan a CIDR reconciliation and route governance document (we can supply a template); also consider using Transit Gateway if you foresee expanding to multiple VPCs.
- We recommend starting with PrivateLink for PCI paths + peering for ingestion. Run a two-week synthetic load to verify peering throughput before shifting critical flows.

Next steps I can drive: share a route governance checklist, propose a Transit Gateway pilot if you have >2 VPCs, and schedule the synthetic load.

—Marcus
Head of Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
